title: Festive Fare: Cranberry Pistachio Fudge.
subtitle: Make-at-home treats to gift or enjoy!
description: Our seasonal collection of giftable treats is so delicious, you'll want to keep them all for yourself. But why not share the sweet fudgy love? Pack them into little jars or boxes and give to a friend, or serve with coffee after your festive lunch or dinner.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Grease and line a 10cm x 20cm loaf pan with baking paper, extending the paper 5cm above the sides. Put the pistachios in a cold small frypan over medium heat. Toast, tossing, for 3-4 mins until evenly golden. Remove from the pan and cool slightly. Halve the pistachios lengthwise.

Start fudge: Put the condensed milk, 110g (½ cup) caster sugar and 20g butter in a small saucepan over low heat. Cook, whisking constantly, for 8-10 mins until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is smooth (see Kitchen 101).

Add mix-ins: Increase the heat to medium-low and bring to a very gentle simmer. Cook, whisking, for 4 mins or until the mixture thickens slightly (see Kitchen 101). Remove the pan from the heat and quickly whisk in the chocolate chips until melted and smooth (the mixture will be quite thick). Stir in the cranberries and half the pistachios.

Pour into pan: Working quickly, spread the fudge into the lined pan (it will already be starting to firm up). Scatter over the remaining pistachios, then smooth the surface with the back of the spoon or spatula.

Set and serve up: Set aside at room temperature for 1 hr or until set (if it's a hot day, set aside to cool slightly, then pop it in the fridge to set). Lift the fudge out of the pan and cut into 18 squares. Enjoy straight away, or store in an airtight container for up to 1 week. Makes 18 pieces (1 per serve).

Kitchen 101s: The mixture can catch on the bottom of the pan and burn easily, so keep the heat low and whisk constantly. ~ Make sure you simmer the fudge mixture for 4 mins: less than that and it won't set in the pan; too long and it will set too hard.
